system_overview: This specification extends the Disk Synod (Disk Paxos) algorithm with a set of hierarchical invariants (HInv1 through HInv6) used for proving that the Disk Synod algorithm correctly implements the abstract Synod consensus specification. It adds auxiliary history variables to track the globally chosen value and the set of all inputs ever proposed, enabling the statement and checking of detailed inductive invariants.
actors_and_components: The same actors as DiskSynod: N processes communicating through shared disks. This module adds two auxiliary tracking variables for verification purposes: a record of the globally chosen consensus value and the accumulated set of all input values ever proposed by any process.
state_variables: All state variables from the DiskSynod specification (input, output, disk blocks, phase, local disk block, disks written, blocks read), plus: (1) A chosen value: initially a no-output indicator, set to the first value any process outputs and never changed afterward. (2) A set of all inputs: accumulates every input value any process has ever had, including after restarts.
initial_state: Same as DiskSynod, plus: the chosen value starts as the no-output indicator. The all-inputs set is initialized to the set of initial inputs across all processes.
actions: The next-state relation wraps the DiskSynod next-state relation, additionally updating: (1) The chosen value: if no value is chosen yet and some process produces output, the output of that process becomes the chosen value; otherwise the chosen value is unchanged. (2) The all-inputs set: augmented with any new input values from all processes.
safety_properties: Six hierarchical invariants are defined: HInv1 (type invariant): All variables have correct types. HInv2 (block invariants): All blocks associated with a process have ballots from that process's ballot set, ballot consistency (zero ballot if and only if no-input indicator), master ballot is at least as large as ballot, inputs come from the accumulated input set, and phase-specific constraints on disks written, blocks read, and block values. HInv3 (read consistency): If two processes in phases 1 or 2 have each read the other's block from the same disk, then at least one of them has the current version. HInv4 (ballot dominance): A non-phase-0 process's master ballot dominates all its blocks' ballots, and every majority set of disks contains a disk where the process's stored block has been superseded. HInv5 (value agreement): A phase-2 process either has the unique value at its ballot (no higher-ballot block disagrees) or has been superseded on a majority of disks. HInv6 (chosen value safety): If a value has been chosen, it satisfies the value-chosen predicate (a majority of disks lock it in), and all process outputs are either that value or the no-output indicator.
model_bounds: Same constants as DiskSynod must be instantiated. For model checking, the invariants are checked as state predicates.
additional_assumptions: This module extends DiskSynod and inherits all its assumptions. The hierarchical invariants are intended to be proven inductively: each invariant depends on the previous ones. A majority set type is defined for use in the invariants.
